title: Future Builders Refugee Organization
description: FBRO is a refugee-led community organization in Kakuma, Kenya, empowering youth, supporting livelihoods, peacebuilding, and environmental protection.
body: Building hope, empowering futures. Future Builders Refugee Organization is a refugee-led community organization in Kakuma, Kenya, working with refugees and host communities for peace, self-reliance and sustainable livelihoods. Our programs Community-led Residents help identify problems, plan activities and run local solutions. Read more → Seven program areas From peacebuilding and livelihoods to environment, health, education and culture. Read more → Open to partners NGOs, donors, CBOs, government institutions, and youth and women groups are welcome. Read more → Communities understand their challenges best. FBRO was founded in 2024 in Kakuma Refugee Camp by refugees who wanted to respond to the everyday challenges facing their communities: unemployment, few opportunities for young people, poverty, conflict, environmental problems, and limited access to education and skills. We involve community members in identifying problems, planning activities and carrying out local solutions, working closely with youth groups, women groups, community leaders and other refugee-led organizations. title: About Us
description: Learn about FBRO, a refugee-led CBO founded in 2024 in Kakuma Refugee Camp. Background, vision, mission, objectives, and community approach.
body: About FBRO A refugee-led community-based organization founded in 2024 in Kakuma Refugee Camp, Kenya. Why FBRO exists Many families in Kakuma Refugee Camp continue to face social and economic challenges that affect their daily lives. Young people often lack opportunities for skills training and income generation, while vulnerable families struggle to meet basic needs. FBRO was started by refugees who wanted to respond to these everyday challenges: unemployment, lack of opportunities for youth, poverty, conflict, environmental problems, and limited access to education and skills development. It was formed by community members who believed that local communities can create positive change when people work together and support one another. Since its founding, FBRO has mobilized volunteers and community members to take part in activities that promote peacebuilding, youth empowerment, environmental protection, education, and livelihood support. Our vision A peaceful, empowered, and self-reliant community where refugees and host communities live with dignity and hope. title: Our Programs
description: FBRO runs seven community programs in Kakuma: peacebuilding, livelihood support, youth skills, education, conservation, health, and cultural unity.
body: Our programs Seven areas of work, planned and carried out with refugees and host community members. Peacebuilding and social cohesion FBRO brings together refugees and host community members through peace dialogues, community discussions, sports activities, and awareness campaigns that promote unity and peaceful coexistence. Livelihood support We support vulnerable families and youth through poultry keeping, crop farming, and other small income-generating activities that help improve household income and food security. Youth empowerment and skills development FBRO supports youth and women through mentorship, leadership activities, vocational skills training, and entrepreneurship awareness programs that help build confidence and self-reliance. Education and community awareness We encourage education and learning through mentorship activities, awareness campaigns, and community discussions that promote personal growth and the importance of education. Environmental conservation FBRO works with community members to protect the environment through tree planting, environmental awareness activities, and promotion of proper waste management practices. title: Get Involved & Partner
description: Partner with FBRO in Kakuma: NGOs, CBOs, donors, and volunteer groups can collaborate on refugee livelihoods, youth empowerment, and peace initiatives.
body: Get involved Partnerships and teamwork help create stronger and more sustainable impact in the community. Partner with FBRO FBRO welcomes collaboration with organizations and groups that share our commitment to refugees and vulnerable host communities in Kakuma. Tell us about your organization and the program area you are interested in, and we will reply. Our work is led by community members, so we look for partners who want to support local leadership and practical, community-driven programs. We welcome NGOs and humanitarian organizations Refugee-led organizations Community-based organizations (CBOs) Government institutions Donors and development partners Youth and women groups Take part in our activities FBRO mobilizes volunteers and community members to take part in peacebuilding, youth empowerment, environmental protection, education, and livelihood activities. If you would like to ask how to take part, use the form or contact us directly.
